title: OS Midterm Drill
heading: Midterm Drill
lede: Seven past midterm papers, one tab each. Pick an answer to see at once whether it is right. Every answer has a short explanation, and the few answers worth double-checking are flagged.
foot: Questions are typed from the photos in your seven exam PDFs. The papers have no answer key, so the answers were worked out here. The exception is the Nov 2023 paper, where the answers circled on the paper are used. Drawing and written questions are left out. Progress is saved in this browser only.

questions.group: Dr. Mostafa · Q1 choose the answer
questions.text: ......... program is loaded at power-up or reboot.
questions.why: The bootstrap program is the first code that runs when the computer starts (it lives in ROM/firmware). It initializes the hardware and then loads the OS kernel.

questions.group: Dr. Mostafa · Q1 choose the answer
questions.text: Software may trigger an interrupt by executing a special operation called a .........
questions.why: A trap (exception) is a software-generated interrupt, and a program triggers one by executing a system call. Hardware triggers interrupts by sending a signal to the CPU over the bus.

questions.group: Dr. Mostafa · Q1 choose the answer
questions.text: ......... is a technology that allows operating systems to run as applications within other operating systems.
questions.why: Virtualization lets a guest OS run as an application inside a host OS, with a virtual machine manager (VMM) providing the service.

questions.group: Dr. Mostafa · Q1 choose the answer
questions.text: ......... consists of everything below the system-call interface and above the physical hardware.
questions.why: The kernel is the core of the OS. It is the one program running at all times, and it covers everything between the system-call interface and the hardware.

questions.group: Dr. Mostafa · Q1 choose the answer
questions.text: Main memory and ........ are only storage CPU can access directly.
questions.why: The CPU can directly access only registers and main memory. Disks and CD-ROMs must be loaded into main memory first.

questions.group: Dr. Mostafa · Q2 true or false
questions.text: The main function of the operating system is to provide an interface between hardware and application programs used by users.
questions.why: True. The OS acts as an intermediary between the user and application programs on one side and the computer hardware on the other.

questions.group: Dr. Mostafa · Q2 true or false
questions.text: Process is considered as a passive entity while program is considered as an active entity.
questions.why: False, it is the other way round. A program is passive (a file on disk) and a process is active (a program in execution).

questions.group: Dr. Mostafa · Q2 true or false
questions.text: The main components of a computer systems are: Processor – Registers – I/O Modules – Main Memory.
questions.why: Treated as False. A computer system is usually divided into four components: hardware, operating system, application programs and users. The list in the statement also puts registers on their own and leaves out the system bus. Check your slides if your instructor defines components differently.

questions.group: Dr. Mostafa · Q2 true or false
questions.text: Timesharing (multitasking) is logical extension in which CPU switches jobs so frequently that users can interact with each job while it is running, creating interactive computing.
questions.why: True. This is the standard definition of timesharing (multitasking). Response time should be under one second.

questions.group: Dr. Mostafa · Q2 true or false
questions.text: Cloud computing delivers computing, storage, even apps as a service across a network.
questions.why: True. Cloud computing is a logical extension of virtualization that delivers computing, storage and even applications as a service across a network.

questions.text: To access the services of the operating system, the interface is provided by the ______.
questions.why: System calls are the programming interface to the services of the OS. Programs usually reach them through an API.

questions.text: Where is the operating system placed in the memory?
options: either low or high memory (depending on the location of interrupt vector)
questions.why: The OS can sit in low or high memory. It depends on where the interrupt vector is located.

questions.text: Swapping ______ be done when a process has pending I/O, or has to execute I/O operations only into operating system buffers.
questions.why: A process with pending I/O into its own memory cannot be swapped out. If the I/O goes only into OS buffers, the swap is possible, so swapping maybe done.

questions.text: The operating system is responsible for?
questions.why: Disk management includes disk initialization, booting from disk and bad-block recovery, so all three are OS responsibilities.

questions.text: The ______ presents a uniform device-access interface to the I/O subsystem, much as system calls provide a standard interface between the application and the operating system.
questions.why: Each device driver hides the details of its controller and gives the I/O subsystem a uniform interface to the device.

questions.text: Whenever a process needs I/O to or from a disk it issues a ______.
options: system call to the operating system
questions.why: Only the OS (in kernel mode) may perform I/O, so a process asks for it with a system call to the operating system.

questions.text: The ______ program initializes all aspects of the system, from CPU registers to device controllers and the contents of main memory, and then starts the operating system.
questions.why: The bootstrap program initializes the CPU registers, device controllers and memory contents, and then loads and starts the OS kernel.

questions.text: Which of the following programs runs all the time on the computer?
questions.why: The kernel is the one program running at all times on the computer. The other programs run only when they are needed.

questions.text: Which of the following contains the addresses of all the service routines?
questions.why: The interrupt vector holds the addresses of all the interrupt service routines, indexed by interrupt number.

questions.text: Which of the following are used by Linux kernel as data structures?
questions.why: The Linux kernel uses all of them: linked lists, stacks and queues, balanced binary search trees, hash functions and maps, and bitmaps.

questions.text: Which of the following computing environments place rigid time requirements on the operation of a processor or the flow of data?
questions.why: A real-time embedded system has well-defined, fixed time constraints. Processing must finish within them, or the result is wrong.

questions.text: Which is the Linux operating system?
questions.why: Linux (GNU/Linux) is a free and open-source OS, released under the GNU Public License.

questions.text: Which of the following operating systems do you use for a client-server network?
questions.why: Windows 2000 is the usual keyed answer, since it had server editions built for client-server networks while XP and Mac are mainly client systems. The question is weak, because Linux can act as a server too.

questions.text: Which program runs first after booting the computer and loading the GUI?
questions.why: The login (authentication) step runs first, so the system knows who the user is before it shows the desktop or file manager.

questions.text: Which of the following operating system runs on the server?
questions.why: A network operating system runs on a server and gives it the ability to manage data, users, groups, security and applications.

questions.text: What type of memory stores data in a swap file on a hard drive?
questions.why: Virtual memory lets a process run without being completely in RAM. It uses a swap file on the hard drive as an extension of main memory.

questions.text: Buffer is a ______.
questions.why: A buffer is a temporary area that holds data while it is being transferred between two devices, or between a device and an application.

questions.why: Error detection is an OS service. The OS must handle hardware, I/O device and network errors, so all three examples count.

questions.text: If a process fails, most operating system write the error information to a ______.

questions.text: Cascading termination refers to the termination of all child processes if the parent process terminates ______.
questions.why: With cascading termination, if a parent process terminates, all of its children are terminated as well, whether the parent ended normally or abnormally.
questions.ref: Circled on the paper · Process termination

questions.text: The portion of the process scheduler in an operating system that dispatches processes is concerned with ______.
options: assigning ready processes to waiting queue
assigning running processes to blocked queue
questions.why: The dispatcher is the part of the scheduler that gives the CPU to the process that was selected, that is, it assigns ready processes to the CPU.

questions.text: Context switching is part of
questions.why: A context switch happens inside interrupt handling. The handler saves the state of the running process and reloads the state of the next one.
questions.ref: Circled on the paper · Context switch

questions.text: Purpose of Cooperating processes is ......
questions.why: Cooperating processes exist for information sharing, computation speed-up, modularity and convenience, so all of the options apply.

questions.text: In a timeshare operating system, when the time slot assigned to a process is completed, the process switches from the current state to?
questions.why: When the time slice (quantum) ends, the OS preempts the running process and puts it back in the ready queue. It is not blocked, because it is not waiting for anything, and it has not finished.

questions.text: For real time operating systems, interrupt latency should be ......
questions.why: Interrupt latency can never be exactly zero, because the CPU must finish the current instruction and save its state. A real-time OS keeps it as small and as predictable as possible.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a type of operating system?
questions.why: Batch, real-time and distributed systems are all types of OS. There is no type called sequential.

questions.text: Multitasking in operating systems allows for:
options: Multiple users to share a single device
A single user to perform multiple tasks at one time
Devices to run without an OS
questions.why: Multitasking switches the CPU between jobs so quickly that one user can run several tasks at the same time.

questions.text: In a multiprocessing system, processes:
options: Are executed one at a time
questions.why: A multiprocessing system has two or more CPUs, so processes can truly run in parallel, one per CPU. Resource sharing is a benefit, but parallel execution is the defining property. Option B is also partly true, so double-check with your notes.

questions.text: Context switching is:
options: The process of saving and restoring the state of a CPU so that multiple processes can share a single CPU resource
The act of switching between different applications by the user
questions.why: A context switch saves the state of the running process (into its PCB) and restores the state of another, so many processes can share one CPU.

questions.text: Most operating systems (including UNIX, Linux, and Windows) identify processes according to a unique ______.
questions.why: UNIX, Linux and Windows identify every process with a unique process identifier (PID).

questions.text: Suppose that a process is in “Blocked” state waiting for some I/O service. When the service is completed, it goes to the ....
questions.why: When the I/O completes, a blocked process moves to the ready state and waits for the CPU. It never goes straight to running.

questions.text: A process stack does not contain
questions.why: The stack holds function parameters, local variables and return addresses. The PID of a child process is not part of that list.

questions.text: If a process fails, most operating system write the error information to a
questions.why: When a process fails, the OS writes the error information to a log file. It may also save a core dump for debugging.

questions.text: In operating system, each process has its own
options: pending alarms, signals and signal handlers
questions.why: Each process has its own address space and global variables, its own open files, and its own pending alarms, signals and signal handlers, so all three apply.

questions.text: Which of the following Operating systems use multiple central processors to serve multiple real-time applications and multiple users?
questions.why: A distributed OS uses multiple central processors to serve multiple real-time applications and multiple users.

questions.text: Which of the following Operating systems runs on a server and provides the server the capability to manage data, users, groups, etc?
questions.why: A network operating system runs on a server and gives it the ability to manage data, users, groups, security and applications.

questions.text: What is a bootstrap program?
options: It is the first code that is executed when the computer system is started
It is the program that helps in restarting the system
It is just a simple program like we have other programs in a system
questions.why: The bootstrap program is the first code executed when the computer starts. It initializes the system and loads the OS kernel.

questions.text: Instructions are executed in which state?
questions.why: A process executes instructions only in the running state. In ready it waits for the CPU, and in waiting it waits for an event.

questions.text: If processes don't fit in memory, moving them in and out to run is called.
questions.why: Swapping moves processes between main memory and the backing store (disk) so that more processes can run than fit in memory at once.

questions.text: Which of the following operating systems is non interactive?
questions.why: A batch system collects jobs and runs them in groups, and the user cannot interact with a job while it runs. Multitasking and multi-user systems are interactive.

questions.text: The ____ of a process contains temporary data such as function parameters, return addresses, and local variables.
questions.why: A process in memory has a text section (code), a data section (globals), a heap, and a stack. The stack holds function parameters, return addresses and local variables.

questions.text: Which of the following state transitions is NOT possible?
questions.why: After the event it was waiting for, a process goes from waiting to ready, never straight to running. Only the scheduler dispatches a ready process to the CPU.

questions.text: A blocking send() and blocking receive() is known as a(n).
questions.why: When both send() and receive() are blocking, the sender and the receiver wait for each other and meet at the exchange. This is called a rendezvous.

questions.text: The child process completes execution, but the parent keeps executing, then the child process is known as
questions.why: A child that has finished while its parent keeps running, without the parent calling wait() yet, is a zombie. An orphan is a child whose parent has terminated.

questions.text: To access the services of the operating system, the interface is provided by the ______.
questions.why: System calls are the programming interface to the services of the OS. Programs usually reach them through an API.

questions.text: Message passing system allows processes to ______.
options: communicate with each other without sharing the same address space
communicate with one another by resorting to shared data
name the recipient or sender of the message
questions.why: Message passing lets processes communicate and synchronize without sharing an address space, by sending and receiving messages through the OS.

questions.text: The ______ presents a uniform device-access interface to the I/O subsystem, much as system calls provide a standard interface between the application and the operating system.
questions.why: Each device driver hides the details of its controller and gives the I/O subsystem a uniform interface to the device.

options: system call to the operating system
questions.why: Only the OS (in kernel mode) may perform I/O, so a process asks for it with a system call to the operating system.

questions.text: The link between two processes P and Q to send and receive messages is called ______.
questions.why: To send and receive messages, a communication link must exist between processes P and Q.

questions.text: The ______ program initializes all aspects of the system, from CPU registers to device controllers and the contents of main memory, and then starts the operating system.
questions.why: The bootstrap program initializes the CPU registers, device controllers and memory contents, and then loads and starts the OS kernel.

questions.why: The kernel is the one program running at all times on the computer. The other programs run only when they are needed.

questions.text: Which of the following contains the addresses of all the service routines?
questions.why: The interrupt vector holds the addresses of all the interrupt service routines, indexed by interrupt number.

questions.text: A parent process calling ______ system call will be suspended until children processes terminate.
questions.why: A parent that calls wait() is suspended until one of its children terminates.

questions.text: Which of the following computing environments place rigid time requirements on the operation of a processor or the flow of data?
questions.why: A real-time embedded system has well-defined, fixed time constraints. Processing must finish within them, or the result is wrong.

questions.text: What is a Process Control Block?
questions.why: The PCB is a kernel data structure that stores everything the OS needs about a process: its state, program counter, CPU registers, scheduling and memory information.

questions.text: Which program runs first after booting the computer and loading the GUI?
questions.why: The login (authentication) step runs first, so the system knows who the user is before it shows the desktop or file manager.

questions.text: What type of memory stores data in a swap file on a hard drive?
questions.why: Virtual memory lets a process run without being completely in RAM. It uses a swap file on the hard drive as an extension of main memory.

questions.text: What is the objective of multiprogramming?
options: Have a process running at all time
Have multiple programs waiting in a queue ready to run
questions.why: Multiprogramming keeps several jobs in memory so the CPU always has one to run. The objective is to increase CPU utilization.

questions.text: Buffer is a ______.
questions.why: A buffer is a temporary area that holds data while it is being transferred between two devices, or between a device and an application.

questions.text: Which of the following is not the state of a process?
questions.why: The process states are new, ready, running, waiting and terminated. There is no state called old.

questions.text: When several processes access the same data concurrently and the outcome of the execution depends on the particular order in which the access takes place is called ______.
questions.why: This is a race condition. The result depends on the order in which the processes access the shared data.

questions.text: A process stack does not contain
questions.why: The stack holds function parameters, local variables and return addresses. The PID of a child process is not part of that list.

questions.text: The address of the next instruction to be executed by the current process is provided by the ______.
questions.why: The program counter holds the address of the next instruction the process will execute.
